title: Return from Texas: Pajeaud, the Famous Door, the Eureka and rock and roll bands
summary: Back from Texas, Williams played with Pajeaud, at the Famous Door, with the Eureka band and a rock and roll band.

bands.name: O'Vell Anderson's rock and roll band

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who did you play with? What was the name of the band?

First band was Buddy. When you came back from Texas? Oh, when I come back from Texas. Not California. Oh, I was talking about California. When I first came back from Texas. Oh, boy. It was a good while before I played with anybody. So I was kind of sick. See, I went, Pajio come at me, I played with him. He had a little man. Played with Pajio. Played with him a little over a year, I think. Then I went in there. What Hip Gimler's place named?

The famous two. Me, Badlacks, Lewis Givens, Poire. Went there two nights a week. See, them boys was playing there, you know. And Smiley and Joe and Thed O, they were playing one night, you see. I mean, they were playing there all the week. Monday night, the white band would be off. And Sunday night, Thed O and them would be off with Badlacks. I played there them two nights. Played there for about a year. And then I went with, with, uh, uh, uh, O'Vell Anderson's rock and roll band. I played with them about two or three years. I played with them.
I don't know if you get that straight. Pajio and Harold, I believe.
I think Harold was playing out there already.

Yeah, I think. I just remember now. Cause he, you know, he didn't have no organized band, you know, see. He had a high-definite fella. Oh, I see. Played down at his place on Claiborne Street a while with him. You know, they used to play down on Claiborne and parties that did at the Overpass. Yeah, I know, the Harmony Inn. Yeah, played down there. Played down there a while with him. And I joined the Eureka band when that boy got his legs cut off, you know.

That was, uh, 52. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. And after I got, stopped playing with her, I played with her until 55, I think. 55 or 56. And who else did I started playing with after that? Some band in school. Very good band. You been in a rock and roll band or...? No. No, it wasn't a rock and roll. I enjoyed playing with her. I was a nice little rock and roll band. Mm-hmm.
Mm-hmm. Got plenty of work. Used to play at the Redemptionist. Regular.
And we used to play at the... ...and we used to play at the...

You know, at that gym up there. Constant and Marlon. Played there every Friday night for about three years. Mm-hmm. About three years, every Friday, played there, all holidays that we could take. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
